provenance: covered_text is the same selection on all seventeen pages, read back from pdftotext on base.pdf. The page_label column was resolved from the catalog's /PageLabels by hand and re-derived programmatically. The quad invariant was measured from a copy of base.pdf with /Rotate and /CropBox stripped, so that pdftotext's frame was unambiguously the media box -- with them present, pdftotext reports in the display frame, which shifts with rotation and gives coordinates outside the page for the 90 and 270 pages. No producer file existed when this was written.
matching: Match by the [[PGnn]] sentinel in covered_text. Every item has covered text, so none falls back to page, subtype and comment. An extracted text containing a sentinel other than its own fails regardless of the rest of the string -- which here also catches a quad that landed on the wrong page.
author_policy: author is null for every item: any value passes. Producers commonly override the author with the system user name.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG01]]
annotations.notes: The control. It separates a systematic error, which breaks every page, from a combination-specific one, which breaks only some. IF PG01 FAILS, NOTHING ELSE IN THIS FAMILY MEANS ANYTHING -- fix it before reading any other result. Also the only page with no page label: it falls before the first /PageLabels range, which is legal.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG02]]
annotations.notes: Rotation alone. Establishes the baseline that PG06 and PG10 are measured against; passing here and failing there is a combination defect, not missing rotation support.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG03]]
A highlight sits on this page [[PG04]]
annotations.notes: Rotation alone. Compare PG14, which is the same rotation written as -90.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG05]]
annotations.notes: The crop offset alone. The text does not move in user space; only the page box does.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG06]]
annotations.notes: THE POINT OF THE FAMILY. Rotation and the crop offset adjust the same coordinates, and an implementation that gets each right alone can still combine them with the wrong sign. pdfannots2json subtracts CropBox from MediaBox on one rotation and MediaBox from CropBox on another; only a page with both features set shows it.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG07]]
annotations.notes: See PG06. All four rotations are present because the defect shape is a sign error at ONE rotation, and two of four would find it only by luck.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG08]]
A highlight sits on this page [[PG09]]
annotations.notes: Same page size as PG01 with the origin moved off zero. Probes whether coordinates are treated as absolute or origin-relative.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG10]]
annotations.notes: The PG06 trap with the offset coming from a different key. A tool can special-case /CropBox and still get the origin wrong, or the reverse.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG11]]
A highlight sits on this page [[PG12]]
A highlight sits on this page [[PG13]]
annotations.notes: Two offsets from two different keys have to compose. A tool that handles either alone can still add them twice, or once.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG14]]
annotations.notes: ISO 32000-1 requires /Rotate to be a multiple of 90; it does not require it to be in [0,360). A tool that switches on the raw value, or divides by 90 without normalising, fails here and passes PG04. WEAKLY EVIDENCED: the spec permits it and the normalisation question is real, but no producer has been observed writing a negative rotation. Run tools/survey.py over a real library.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG15]]
annotations.notes: A SILENT ONE. /MediaBox is inheritable (ISO 32000-1 Table 30) and this page omits it. A tool reading the page dictionary only has no page size and no error: data loss that looks like a clean run. Well evidenced from the reader side -- poppler, pdf.js, pdfium and pdfannots2json all implement the /Parent walk, and qpdf ships pushInheritedAttributesToPage() to flatten it away.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG16]]
annotations.notes: The same silent path for /Rotate, which is inheritable too. Most implementations look up inheritable attributes through one generic helper, so a tool that special-cases /MediaBox passes PG15 and fails here. THE WEAKEST-EVIDENCED PAGE IN THE FAMILY: the spec permits it and readers implement the walk generically, but no producer has been observed writing it. If tools/survey.py never finds one, this belongs in tests/structure.

annotations.covered_text: A highlight sits on this page [[PG17]]
annotations.notes: A negative case. Print-ready PDFs from publishers routinely carry /TrimBox and /BleedBox alongside /CropBox, and a tool reaching for the wrong box mislocates every quad on the page. /CropBox is inset 20pt and /TrimBox 40pt, so choosing /TrimBox is off by exactly 20pt in both directions rather than subtly wrong.

quad_invariant: Every page carries the SAME sentence in the SAME place, and /QuadPoints are in default user space regardless of /Rotate. A correct producer file therefore has near-identical quads on all seventeen pages: x = [85.0, 263.2], y = [693.9, 703.6]. That is the operational definition of the selection and check.py tests it. Note the box is the SELECTION, which stops at the sentinel -- not the whole typeset line, which runs 247pt further to '...so the quad has'.
page_naming: The catalog names the pages, and the numbering a paper uses is the numbering a citation must use. physical 1 has NO label; 2-4 are i, ii, iii; 5-10 are 1-6; 11-14 are A-D; 15-17 all read 'App-'. Four styles plus two hazards: a page before the first /Nums range is legal and unlabelled, and a range with a prefix and no /S is legal and gives every page in it the SAME label. Page labels are neither unique nor always present. Which of page and page_label belongs in the output is a POLICY question, not a defect, but they must not be confused: a tool reporting physical numbers agrees with the labels nowhere except by coincidence.
new_fields: page_label and attributes are not in the tests/basic schema and the harness ignores both. page_label is the assertion this family adds and needs harness support; attributes is documentation, so that a failure names the combination without cross-referencing base.tex.

diagnosis.PG01 fails: a systematic error. Stop and fix it; every other result in the family is meaningless until it passes.
diagnosis.PG02-PG04 fail, PG01 passes: /Rotate is not being read at all.
diagnosis.PG05 fails, PG01 passes: /CropBox is not being read at all.
diagnosis.PG02 and PG05 pass, any of PG06-PG08 fai: the rotation and crop offsets are combined with the wrong sign. The failing rotation names which branch. This is the pdfannots2json defect shape and is specific and reportable, NOT 'rotation is unsupported'.
diagnosis.PG09 fails alone: coordinates are treated as absolute; the media box origin is not subtracted, or is subtracted twice.
diagnosis.PG09 and PG02-PG04 pass, any of PG10-PG1: the same sign error as PG06-PG08 with the offset coming from /MediaBox instead of /CropBox.
diagnosis.PG05 and PG09 pass, PG13 fails: the two offsets compose wrongly -- added twice, or only once.
diagnosis.PG15 fails or is dropped: no /Parent walk for inheritable page attributes.
diagnosis.PG15 passes, PG16 fails: the /Parent walk exists but is special-cased to /MediaBox rather than generic over inheritable keys.
diagnosis.PG17 fails, PG05 passes: the wrong page box was chosen. An error of exactly 20pt in both directions means /TrimBox.
diagnosis.all seventeen fail by the same amount: not seventeen transform errors. Suspect the quad frame or the fixture: check.py has a guard for this and names it.

comparison: Compared exactly. There are no per-producer expectation files, no overrides and no variant lists: this file states what the document means, so a producer whose file cannot yield it is a finding to document, and a shortfall in our extractor is a bug to fix.
extractor_options: No option moves anything in this family. No target contains a ligature, an accent or a hyphen, so --keep-ligatures and --keep-hyphens are both inert. That is deliberate: a coordinate result read off a string that moved under a flag would be unreadable. If page numbering ever becomes an option axis -- physical against label -- all seventeen items move with it and page_naming above is the specification.
failure_policy: A failing item is a tracked defect, in our extractor or in the producer. See PRODUCERS.md for observed producer behaviour. Nothing there relaxes this file.
order_policy: No item has an undefined order: one annotation per page, seventeen pages, so page order alone determines the sequence. Ordering WITHIN a page is not exercised here at all.
silent_pass_risks: Three. First, the annotator cannot see which frame the quads were written in -- a viewer that helpfully subtracts the crop inset, or writes quads in the rotated display frame, produces a file that looks perfect on screen and is wrong in exactly the ways this family measures, with the failure landing on our extractor. Run check.py on every producer file before recording anything. Second, make.py must be run after pdflatex or PG15 and PG16 are duplicates of PG01 and PG02 and pass without testing inheritance; make.py --check verifies the whole grid and exits non-zero. Third, expect skips: several viewers cannot annotate a rotated page at all, which is data about the producer rather than a failure, and check.py lists the pages it found nothing on.
status_field: status, notes, attributes, page_label, quad_invariant, page_naming, new_fields, diagnosis and silent_pass_risks are documentation or pending harness support. The harness deserialises id, page, subtype, covered_text, comment, author and order only, and ignores everything else.
